$E_{Li^{2+}} = 2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times 9 = 19.62 \times 10^{-18}\text{ J atom}^{-1}$

$19.62 \times 10^{-18} = 1.962 \times 10^{-17}\text{ J atom}^{-1}$.

question.latex: What is the ratio of wave number of first line $lowest energy line$ of Balmer series of H atomic spectrum to first line of its Brackett series?

explanation.unicode:
Wave number bar{nu} is given by the Rydberg formula: bar{nu} = R_H left( (1/n_1²) - (1/n_2²) right).
For the first line of the Balmer series, n_1 = 2 and n_2 = 3:
bar{nu}_{Balmer} = R_H left( (1/2²) - (1/3²) right) = R_H left( (1/4) - (1/9) right) = R_H left( (5/36) right).
For the first line of the Brackett series, n_1 = 4 and n_2 = 5:
bar{nu}_{Brackett} = R_H left( (1/4²) - (1/5²) right) = R_H left( (1/16) - (1/25) right) = R_H left( (9/400) right).
The ratio is frac{bar{nu}_{Balmer}}{bar{nu}_{Brackett}} = (5/36/9/400) = (5 × 400/36 × 9) = (2000/324) = (500/81) = (5/0.81).

For the first line of the Brackett series, n_1 = 4 and n_2 = 5: bar{nu}_{Brackett} = R_H left( (1)/(4^2) - (1)/(5^2) right) = R_H left( (1)/(16) - (1)/(25) right) = R_H left( (9)/(400) right). The ratio is frac{bar{nu}_{Balmer}}{bar{nu}_{Brackett}} = (5/36)/(9/400) = (5 times 400)/(36 times 9) = (2000)/(324) = (500)/(81) = (5)/(0.81).

explanation.latex:
According to the Aufbau principle, electrons fill atomic orbitals in order of increasing energy level. The filling order is $1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p, 4s, 3d, \dots$
The first $18$ electrons fill up to the $3p$ subshell (Argon core: $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6$).
The $19^{\text{th}}$ electron will enter the $4s$ orbital.
For the $4s$ orbital: principal quantum number $n = 4$, azimuthal quantum number $l = 0$, magnetic quantum number $m = 0$, and spin $s = +\frac{1}{2}$ or $-\frac{1}{2}$.

The filling order is 1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p, 4s, 3d, dots The first 18 electrons fill up to the 3p subshell (Argon core: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6). The 19^{text{th}} electron will enter the 4s orbital. For the 4s orbital: principal quantum number n = 4, azimuthal quantum number l = 0, magnetic quantum number m = 0, and spin s = +(1)/(2) or -(1)/(2).
